title: A soft crossing interpolates to a sharp one
claim: Counting colourings of any cubic bipartite signed system, given with any drawing, reduces in polynomial time to counting colourings of cubic bipartite Pfaffian graphs under signings. (1) The cube minus an edge, unsigned, is a dead cap: its count is 3 whatever its two attachments see. (2) The k-snake, k copies of the soft crossing of TWIST-COUNT B (two twisted truncated-octahedron pages) in series, with one capped host line on each wire between junctions, has a crossover-type Hadamard signature with straight entries sigma_1 Lambda^(k-1), sigma_1 = (40000, -1112, 3336, -192), Lambda = (810000, 7506, -22518, -432). (3) Lattice condition: the valuations of Lambda at 5, 139 and 3 separate count vectors, so the squared products are distinct. (4) A long edge (k capped line-point pairs) has colour matrix 3^k M^k, M = [[1, 2], [2, 1]]. (5) Universality: put a k-snake at every crossing (one edge through it as wire A with one capped host line, the other as wire B with one capped host point) and route every edge as a long edge crossed at most once per segment; every instance is Pfaffian (planar host and pages, glued Kasteleyn signing non-colourable); a two-parameter Vandermonde system over snake and long-edge lengths recovers the count with exact crossovers and exact edges. (6) Demonstrated: counts of signed K3,3 systems (the smallest non-Pfaffian graph) recovered exactly from four counts of certified Pfaffian instances, and an exact edge recovered from long edges.
failure_conditions: A cap whose count depends on its attachments.
A snake whose Hadamard signature has a nonzero turning entry or straight entries off sigma_1 Lambda^(k-1).
Two count vectors with equal squared products of Lambda.
An instance that fails the Pfaffian certificate.
A recovered K3,3 count that differs from the direct count.
foundation_claim_scope: Polynomial-time Turing reduction from counting on cubic bipartite signed systems to counting on Pfaffian ones. Hardness of the source is ticket B.
